text:
Predicates:
RosesOnTV(x, y) ::: Roses are given out on TV at time y.
OnMonday(y) ::: y is a Monday.
GivenOut(x, y) ::: x is given out on TV at time y.
Bachelor(x) ::: x is on the Bachelor.
Portrays(x, y) ::: show x portrays the lives of real people y.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
BreakingBad ::: Breaking Bad.
Premises:
∀x ∀y ((GivenOut(x, y) ∧ OnMonday(y)) → RosesOnTV(x, y)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x ∀y ((RosesOnTV(x, y)) → ∀z (Bachelor(z) → Portrays(z, x))) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (Portrays(x, y) → RealityTV(x)) ::: Everything portraying the lives of real people is a reality TV show.
¬RealityTV(BreakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
∃x ∃y (RosesOnTV(x, y) ∧ OnMonday(y) ∧ y = 8 pm) ::: Breaking Bad is a TV show in which roses are given out on Monday at 8 pm.
